channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Suspect Arrested in Bishkek for Stealing Money from Mosque Donation Box
item.description: Police in Bishkek have arrested a suspect in connection with the theft of money from a donation box at a mosque. The incident occurred on August 29, when the box was broken into and the funds stolen. A criminal case has been initiated, and the investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Double Uranium Production
item.description: Uzbekistan intends to double its uranium production. The country is a significant producer of the radioactive element, and this expansion is part of its broader energy strategy. Further details on the timeline and specific projects were not immediately available.

item.title: China Successfully Tests Flying Wind Power Station at 4000 Meters
item.description: China has successfully tested its S4000 airborne wind energy system in Yueyang city, Hunan province. The system, capable of operating at altitudes up to 4000 meters, utilizes helium-filled platforms to lift power-generating modules. It harnesses stable high-altitude winds to produce electricity, transmitted to the ground via a special cable. Tests focused on safety and reliability in urban environments.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes SCO Cooperation Against Online Youth Recruitment
item.description: Uzbekistan advocates for enhanced cooperation among SCO intelligence services to combat terrorism, cyberattacks, and the spread of extremist ideology online. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev highlighted the growing use of cyberspace by terrorist organizations for propaganda, recruitment, and fundraising, particularly targeting youth.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Mineral Processing Ambitions Threatened by Water Scarcity
item.description: Kazakhstan's plans to increase domestic mineral processing face significant challenges due to water scarcity. The Shalkiya lead-zinc mine requires substantial water, raising concerns about its impact on agriculture, which already operates under irrigation limits. Investors need assurances on water availability before committing to new projects.

item.title: Kazakhstan Extends Ban on Oil Product Exports for Six Months
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Energy has extended the ban on exporting oil products by road and rail until May 22, 2027. The restriction applies to gasoline, diesel, and certain other products, with exceptions for lubricants, fuel tanks, and humanitarian aid. A separate ban on light distillates and bitumen is in effect until June 30, 2027.

item.title: SCO Plus Security Dialogue Begins in Samarkand on Digital Transformation
item.description: The first expert 'SCO Plus Dialogue on Security' has commenced in Samarkand, focusing on security in the digital transformation era and countering terrorism and extremism with new technologies. The event is chaired by the head of Uzbekistan's State Security Service.

item.title: Uzbekistan Offers to Host Regional UN Counterterrorism Office
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev offered to host a Central Asian office of the United Nations Office of Counter-Terrorism at the Aqaba Process summit in Astana. The proposed office would help Central Asian countries establish channels for reporting terrorist content and detecting terrorist financing. The summit, co-hosted by Kazakhstan and Jordan, focused on how terrorist groups could use artificial intelligence for recruitment and coordination.

item.title: Wife of Tajik Opposition Figure Faces Deportation from Europe to Dushanbe
item.description: The wife of Asadullo Boboev, a member of the Tajik opposition movement extradited from Germany to his homeland, reports she also faces deportation from Germany to Dushanbe. Mastona Fayzulloeva stated that German authorities informed her of her impending deportation two months after her husband and son were sent back. She previously faced deportation in May but it was prevented.

item.title: Kazakhstan Significantly Increases Meat and Metal Exports to Tajikistan
item.description: Kazakhstan has substantially increased its exports of meat and metal products to Tajikistan. Bilateral trade volume reached $1.1 billion in January-September, a 29.5% increase year-on-year. Exports of beef rose 1.7 times to 3.3 thousand tons, while steel bar deliveries grew by 42.3%.

item.title: Stepnogorsk Cancels 21 State Procurements Worth 1.8 Billion Tenge Due to Inflated Estimates
item.description: The Stepnogorsk prosecutor's office has canceled 21 state procurement procedures totaling 1.8 billion tenge due to unjustified cost overruns and inclusion of unnecessary work. Two department heads in the city administration have been disciplined. This action prevented the inefficient spending of 714 million tenge.

item.title: Uzbekistan Considers Revising Customs Duties on Food Products, Reducing Exemptions
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Investments, Industry, and Trade has proposed revising customs exemptions for food and consumer goods. A draft presidential decree suggests extending zero-rate import duties for 45 product categories until 2028, while not extending them for nine groups, including dairy, fruits, confectionery, and beverages. This aims to adjust current benefits expiring in 2027.

item.title: Fake Statement Attributed to Kazakhstan's Sports Minister Circulates Online
item.description: False statements concerning Kazakhstan's stance on Russian hockey players are being spread online, falsely attributed to the Minister of Tourism and Sport, Yerbol Mirzakhmetov. The Center for Combating Disinformation reported that the messages, distributed in Russian, Czech, and English from Eastern and Central European accounts, aim to distort Kazakhstan's official position and increase international tension.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Establish Environmental Control Over Former Uranium Tailings Sites
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has approved a procedure for radioecological monitoring of former uranium production sites and radioactive waste storage facilities after their reclamation. The government aims to ensure the safety of territories previously involved in uranium mining and processing.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Sunflower Pellet Exports More Than Triple in First Nine Months of 2026
item.description: Kazakhstan's exports of sunflower husk pellets surged to 63,200 metric tons in the first nine months of 2026, a 3.56-fold increase year-on-year. Export revenue rose by 515% to $3.4 million, driven by demand from Polish power plants using the pellets as biomass fuel.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Distribute 170 Houses Received from Tajikistan to Batken Residents
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will distribute 170 houses, received from Tajikistan through land exchange, to residents of Batken Oblast. These homes will be provided to citizens who suffered during the 2021-2022 border conflict between Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan. The houses were deemed habitable after the land exchange agreement.

item.title: Cars Account for 60% of Almaty's Emissions, Other Pollutants Identified
item.description: Cars are responsible for approximately 60% of Almaty's emissions, totaling about 113,000 tons annually. The city's ecology department stated that private homes heating with coal and wood, as well as businesses using solid and liquid fuel, also contribute significantly to air pollution, especially in colder months. Natural factors like temperature inversion also play a role.

item.title: Turkish Official Questions Russia's Eligibility for Turkic States Observer Status
item.description: A senior Turkish official has questioned Russia's eligibility for observer status in the Organization of Turkic States (OTS), citing language requirements. The rules, adopted in 2021, mandate that observer countries must recognize a Turkic or related language as a state or official language for nationwide government correspondence. Russia's federal language is Russian, though some regions have Turkic languages.

item.title: Middle Corridor Needs $55 Billion Investment to Become Economic Corridor, World Bank Says
item.description: Developing the Middle Corridor, a route linking China and Europe via Central Asia, requires at least $25 billion for infrastructure and $30.5 billion for complementary projects like logistics centers. The World Bank estimates this could triple Caspian Sea freight by 2040, boosting GDP by 3.3% and creating two million jobs in participating countries.

item.title: National Bank Extends Concessions on Mortgage and Auto Loans
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Bank has extended the exemption from mandatory debt burden coefficient (DBC) requirements for certain loans under the housing savings system and auto-lending. The exemption for housing savings loans will last until December 31, 2029, and for specific auto loans until December 31, 2027.

item.title: Uzbekistan Showcases Innovations at InnoWeek 2026 in Tashkent
item.description: Uzbekistan presented a range of innovations at InnoWeek 2026 in Tashkent, including a remotely controlled firefighting robot, agricultural drones, and student-developed electric vehicles. The firefighting robot, designed to operate up to 800 meters away and withstand high temperatures, is a prototype developed in collaboration with the Ministry of Emergency Situations.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Makerspace Project for Youth Extended for Three More Years
item.description: The Makerspace project in Kazakhstan, offering free training in robotics, programming, and modern technologies to children and youth, will continue for another three years. The US Embassy in Kazakhstan and Chevron have agreed to extend their partnership for this initiative. The project aims to help young people realize their ideas and learn new technologies.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and El Salvador Discuss Creating State Crypto Reserve
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and El Salvador have agreed to enhance cooperation in virtual assets and blockchain technologies, including discussions on establishing a state reserve of digital assets. A memorandum of understanding was signed, focusing on experience exchange in cryptocurrency market regulation, licensing, and supervision. Both sides emphasized the importance of secure storage and management of digital assets.

item.title: Most Kyrgyz Pediatricians Mistakenly Believe Childhood Cancer is Preventable
item.description: A survey in Kyrgyzstan revealed that around 70% of pediatricians incorrectly believe childhood cancer is preventable. Head of pediatric oncology Sultan Stambekov stated that most childhood cancers are not preventable, with genetic changes being the primary cause. He highlighted a lack of awareness among pediatricians regarding childhood oncology and the need for better early detection and referral to specialists.

item.title: Suspect Arrested in Ust-Kamenogorsk for Drug Packaging
item.description: A 20-year-old woman was arrested in Ust-Kamenogorsk, Kazakhstan, on suspicion of packaging drugs for an online store. She was reportedly paid in cryptocurrency for her work. Police found 350 packets of a powdery substance on her and an additional 28 packets and two containers in her rented apartment. The substance was identified as the psychotropic drug α-PVP, totaling 635 grams.

item.title: Comedian Nurlan Sabirov's Almaty Concert Sparks Public Outrage Over Alleged Support for Russian Military
item.description: Comedian Nurlan Sabirov's recent concert in Almaty has ignited a debate on social media. While some fans expressed disappointment at missing tickets, others called for a boycott, citing alleged support for Russian soldiers involved in the Ukraine conflict. The controversy resurfaced after a video showed Sabirov donating motorcycles to a Wagner PMC unit.

item.title: Women Queue for Kazakhstan’s Umai Mortgages Amid Questions Over Affordability
item.description: Women in Almaty and Astana lined up hoping to secure mortgages under Kazakhstan's Umai program, designed to aid homeownership. The rush highlighted challenges women face in the housing market, including a significant gender pay gap, with average female earnings at 72% of men's. Questions remain about the program's affordability for those most in need.

item.title: Astana to Host World Kurash Wrestling Championship for the First Time
item.description: Astana is set to host the World Kurash Wrestling Championship for the first time in its history. This marks a significant event for the sport in the capital city, bringing international attention to kurash wrestling.

item.title: Kazakhstan Halts Oil Shipments Amid Ukraine Drone Attack, Resumes Flow
item.description: Kazakhstan temporarily halted crude oil shipments via the Atyrau-Samara pipeline following a Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian oil refinery. The Energy Ministry announced the resumption of oil flow hours later. Kazakhstan plans to produce 99 million tons of oil this year, potentially exceeding OPEC+ quotas.

item.title: Kazakhstan National Bank Revises Inflation Forecast Upward for 2027
item.description: The National Bank of Kazakhstan has raised its 2027 inflation forecast to 6.5%-8.5% from 5.5%-7.5%, citing concerns over increased government spending and a planned minimum wage hike. The forecast incorporates the impact of the 'People's Construction' program and a rise in minimum wage to 110,000 tenge in January 2027.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Considers Ban on Energy Drink Production and Import
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Japarov has instructed the government to consider banning the production and import of energy drinks due to health risks. He noted significant consumption levels and potential health issues like heart attacks and diabetes. The ban could result in a loss of approximately $17.15 million in tax revenue.

item.title: Uzbekistan expands key China-Europe route highway for freight transport
item.description: Uzbekistan is widening a major highway on the China-Europe route to improve freight transport. A 25-kilometer section of the A380 highway in Karakalpakstan is being expanded from two to four lanes, with completion expected by the end of 2026. A 240-kilometer segment completed in 2024 has already significantly reduced travel times and costs for carriers.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Property Documents Handed to Villagers Who Moved to Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Property documents have been handed over to villagers who moved from Uzbekistan to Kyrgyzstan. Approximately 1,200 residents live in the village of Qorayantoq, where they had previously received Kyrgyz passports. This marks a step in the border settlement process.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Three More Individuals Added to Political Prisoner List
item.description: Three more individuals have been added to the list of political prisoners in Kazakhstan. These include former priest Iakov Vorontsov, activist Gulnaz Serikbaeva, and activist Nurzhan Sembaev. Human rights defenders cited their activism and criticism of state actions as reasons for their designation.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Chairman of State Security Service Addresses SCO Security Dialogue
item.description: Uzbekistan's State Security Service Chairman, Bakhodir Kurbanov, stated that digital civilization's achievements should not become tools for terrorism. He emphasized the need for joint efforts to ensure their use for peace, security, and sustainable development. Kurbanov noted over 49,000 extremist internet resources were identified in Uzbekistan in 2026.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes Opening UN Counter-Terrorism Office in Tashkent
item.description: Shavkat Mirziyoyev attended the Aqaba Process meeting on artificial intelligence security in Astana. He emphasized the growing threats and the importance of the Aqaba Process. Mirziyoyev highlighted that while AI offers opportunities, it also presents new risks, stressing education and human potential as crucial for security.

item.title: Israel's UN Envoy: Idea to Attack Iran Originated from US, Israel Supported Decision
item.description: Israel's ambassador to the UN, Danny Dannon, responded to US Vice President Joe Biden's accusations regarding war against Iran, stating that the idea to attack Iran originated from the US. He asserted that Israel merely supported the decision of its American allies. The statement clarifies Israel's position on potential military action against Iran.

item.title: Turkmenistan in preliminary talks with foreign companies for data center development
item.description: Turkmenistan is holding preliminary discussions with foreign companies to establish data centers for high-performance computing. Deputy Energy Minister Serdar Saparow announced this at the CIET-2026 international conference in Ashgabat. Such projects could utilize surplus electricity, attract investment, and develop technological infrastructure. Details on companies, locations, and timelines were not disclosed.

item.title: Iran submits nuclear proposal to US via Qatar, awaiting response to demands
item.description: A senior Iranian official revealed that Iran has sent a nuclear proposal to the United States through Qatar. The proposal is contingent on Washington meeting Tehran's seven demands, which include lifting sanctions and releasing frozen assets. Mediators are intensifying efforts to de-escalate tensions amid fears of renewed conflict.

item.title: Uzbekistan Reports 14% Increase in Internet Resources with Extremist and Terrorist Content
item.description: The number of internet resources with extremist and terrorist characteristics in Uzbekistan has increased by 14%. The head of the State Security Service noted that terrorist and extremist organizations are actively using digital technologies to spread their ideology, recruit supporters, and finance and prepare for terrorist attacks.
